channel.description: Latest articles from Alaska Watchman – Bias and Credibility (alaskawatchman.com)

item.title: OPINION: Fear-based distrust of new energy projects holds Alaska back
item.description: Alaska’s energy future is on the line, and too often our first instinct is to say no. Not a careful, measured no, but a reflexive, default position that shuts the door before the facts ever get a fair hearing. That fear-based approach does not protect Alaska.

item.title: FLIP-FLOP: Murkowski decries move to bar men from female sports, then votes for it anyway
item.description: U.S. Sen. Lisa Murkowski is walking a fine, often contradictory line as she continues to air her grievances with a GOP-backed effort to strengthen election integrity and protect women’s sports from gender-confused men.

item.title: Supreme Court case could quash Alaska policy of letting ballots arrive weeks after Election Day
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court is set to hear oral arguments on March 23 in a case that could upend election rules in more than a dozen states, including in Alaska, by determining whether federal law requires ballots to be received by Election Day - not just cast or postmarked by then.

item.title: Gubernatorial candidates on unlocking Alaska’s resources & diversifying revenue
item.description: Alaska faces structural deficits due to volatile oil prices and heavy federal reliance. If elected as Alaska’s chief executive, what concrete steps are you willing and able to take to unlock our resources and diversify the state’s revenue stream?

item.title: OPINION: After 5,000 years, Iran faces the ‘knife-edge’ of history
item.description: Driven by a profound sense of history and Persian identity, Iran has emerged as a formidable, yet isolated, regional power. Today, it faces a defining, “knife-edge” moment between success and failure.

item.title: OPINION: SB 64 doesn’t save Alaska’s Ranked-Choice Voting - it exposes it
item.description: Senate Bill 64 is not a rescue plan for ranked-choice voting, nor does it give anyone extra talking points. It is a cleanup bill for Alaska’s election system, maybe the best we have ever seen.

item.title: Do Alaska’s gubernatorial candidates back a statewide sales tax?
item.description: What did Alaska’s gubernatorial candidates say when asked if they would ever support some form of a statewide sales tax?

item.title: Lawmakers advance bill to shield AK librarians who offer sexually explicit books to kids

item.title: UPDATE: Registration now open for newly formed ‘Alaskan Party’
item.description: Two former chairmen of the recently disbanded Alaskan Independence Party (AIP) have announced that the re-named “Alaskan Party” is now an officially recognized “political group.”

item.title: U.S. House passes Begich’s bill to cut red tape for Alaska’s rural airports
item.description: By cutting unnecessary federal red tape, we can complete critical runway projects faster, reduce costs, and keep communities connected to essential services like medical care and mail delivery,” Rep. Begich said.
